inventedEvidence.evidence: "Thanks for the update on the vents and coils" — customer never checked or mentioned coils (can't access the back); also "Thanks for letting us know about the fan noise" when customer only said it was "running a lot"

rationale: The assistant ran a generic script that ignored key evidence: it never asked for the model number, never followed up on the power cut or suggested the obvious low-cost full defrost, and never adapted to the integrated/rented situation (no mention of landlord/letting agent despite the customer saying so in the opener). It concluded 'blocked vents or over-packing' immediately after the customer said the vents were clear, and thanked the customer for updates on 'fan noise' and 'coils' they never gave. The final handoff was safe, honest about uncertainty, part-free and included sensible food-safety advice, so the homeowner ends up pointed at an engineer, but via a weaker route than the landlord escalation the situation required.
